title: [bug] Local dispatch dies on Debian/Ubuntu: 'set -o pipefail' runs under /bin/sh (dash)
description:
LinuxCommands.cleanExec() returns no `shell`, so LocalStrategy.execCommand falls back to Node's `shell: true` = /bin/sh. On Debian/Ubuntu that is dash, which has no 'set -o pipefail'.

buildAgentPromptCommand (src/os/linux.ts:145) emits `set -o pipefail; <cli> | tee <durable>` whenever opts.inv is set. Under dash this aborts immediately:
  /bin/sh: 1: set: Illegal option -o pipefail
and execute_prompt returns reason='nonzero_exit' -> AGENT_DISPATCH_FAILED.

IMPACT: every local Linux member is undispatchable on any distro where /bin/sh is dash. Windows is unaffected (cleanExec returns shell:'powershell.exe'). macOS is unaffected (/bin/sh there honours pipefail).

The code comment at linux.ts:141 already assumes bash ('bash and zsh both honour it') -- the defect is that nothing ever selects bash.

FIX: LinuxCommands.cleanExec should return shell: '/bin/bash'.
REPRO: fleet-sprint on a local Ubuntu member -> planner dispatch fails instantly.

title: Unblock the fleet-sprint deploy phase: 4 installer/binary permission grants are missing
description: Deploy stopped at deploy.md Step 0a in all three cycles of this sprint (and therefore IntegTest never ran, leaving apra-fleet-b4g.1 and apra-fleet-b4g.2 unverified against a deployed build). The merged effective allowlist from .claude/settings.json + .claude/settings.local.json covers node/npm/curl-based steps via the broad Bash(node:*), Bash(npm:*), Bash(curl:*) entries, but has no covering entry for four required prefixes from deploy.md's Permissions section: Bash(*apra-fleet-installer-* install *), Bash(dist/apra-fleet-installer-* install *), Bash(*apra-fleet* start), Bash(*apra-fleet* --version). These are direct invocations of the built dist/apra-fleet-installer-* and $HOME/.apra-fleet/bin/apra-fleet executables, which no npm/node prefix covers. Fix by running compose_permissions to add the four grants to .claude/settings.local.json (the correct per-checkout target -- not a hand-edit, and not a wrapper script, per the repo's 'permission blocks must be surfaced, not routed around' convention). Until this lands every fleet-sprint on this repo burns its deploy and integ phases, so no sprint here can produce deployed-build evidence.

title: Stop kb tools silently anchoring the real project KB at the fleet server process.cwd()
description: src/tools/kb-session-prime.ts:110-114 resolveRepoPath() returns null when the supplied repo_path does not exist on this host, and line 185 passes `?? undefined` to getKbProviders, which resolves the anchor as `cwd ?? process.cwd()` (src/services/knowledge/kb-providers.ts:86). For a remote member this means the SLUG comes from repo_remote_url (the real shared project KB) while the repoPath ANCHOR becomes the fleet server's own working directory. Reproduced on fix/kb-remote-member-scoping with an isolated APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR against the dist build: cwd=/tmp/.../server-cwd, repo_path='C:\\Users\\member\\work\\repo', repo_remote_url='git@github.com:acme/b4g-cwd.git' -> provider.dbPath=<data>/knowledge/githubcom-acme-b4g-cwd/kb.sqlite but provider.repoPath=/tmp/.../server-cwd. repoPath is load-bearing for the capture basis check and for checkFreshness (src/services/knowledge/sqlite-provider.ts:275-314), so a basis file that happens to exist under the server's cwd is hashed from a tree it does not describe -- the exact silent-corruption mode apra-fleet-b4g.2's description says must never happen ('Do NOT silently fall back to process.cwd()'), now reachable against the REAL shared KB rather than the isolated 'default' one. kb-stats.ts:52 and kb-export.ts:325 have the identical resolveRepoPath-nulls-to-cwd shape and need the same treatment. This is distinct from apra-fleet-b4g.4 (which addresses the anchor BEING the missing path); here the anchor is a valid but WRONG directory, so b4g.4's 'treat a missing path as no anchor' fix does not cover it unless the null-to-cwd fallback is closed at the same time. Settle both in one change and add a regression test asserting provider.repoPath is never process.cwd() when repo_path was supplied but did not validate.

title: Never anchor a KB provider at a repo path that does not exist on this host
description:
getKbProviders (src/services/knowledge/kb-providers.ts:85-100) passes the caller's repo_path straight to createKbProvidersForSlug as the provider's repoPath, with no existence check. Now that apra-fleet-b4g.1 lets a remote member route to the REAL project KB via repo_remote_url, the provider serving that member is anchored at a Windows/remote path that does not exist on the fleet server, and that anchor is load-bearing for freshness.

Reproduced during review: capture a healthy entry from a real local clone of remote R, then call kb_session_prime with repo_path set to a nonexistent remote-style path plus repo_remote_url R. prime (sqlite-provider.ts:1197) calls checkFreshness (sqlite-provider.ts:479-500), which re-hashes every candidate entry's stored basis with cwd set to the bogus repoPath; nothing resolves, basisFullyMatches returns false, and the entries are UPDATEd to stale=1 in the SHARED project DB. kb_list on the local clone then returns 0 results. Up to 10 healthy entries are silently retired per prime call, and every remote-member session begins with a prime.

Capture is already safe by accident (assertCheckableBasis rejects fail-closed at sqlite-provider.ts:318-327), so the work is on the read/sweep side.

Suggested direction: treat a repo path that does not exist on this host as NO anchor -- pass repoPath undefined to SqliteProvider, which unresolvableBasisFiles (sqlite-provider.ts:295-299) already handles as not-checkable -- or explicitly suppress the stale=1 writes in checkFreshness/freshnessSweep when the anchor is missing. Do not silently fall back to process.cwd(): that is the original apra-fleet-b4g.2 corruption mode. Whichever is chosen, keep the (slug, repoPath) cache key correct for the anchor actually used.

Regression tests required: (1) a prime issued with a nonexistent repo_path plus a valid repo_remote_url must leave a healthy entry's stale flag at 0, asserted on the raw row and via kb_list; (2) the same prime from the real local clone must still stale an entry whose basis file genuinely changed, so the fix does not just disable freshness. While here, note that kb_freshness_sweep (src/tools/kb-freshness-sweep.ts:24) calls freshnessSweep() with no root, so it hashes against process.cwd() rather than the provider's repoPath -- a separate, pre-existing inconsistency with checkFreshness that should be settled in the same change.

title: [test] Same-slug different-repoPath providers stay distinct and correctly anchored
description:
File: tests/knowledge/kb-provider-cache-key.test.ts (new), vitest, fixture style of tests/knowledge/kb-repo-isolation.test.ts.

Cover:
1. Two tmpdir clones with the SAME origin remote (so they resolve to one slug) at different paths: getKbProviders(pathA) then getKbProviders(pathB); assert project.repoPath === pathA and === pathB respectively. This fails on the pre-fix tree, where the second call returns the first provider still anchored at pathA -- it is the regression pin.
2. Identical (slug, repoPath): two awaited getKbProviders(pathA) calls return the same object (===); also fire both without awaiting the first and assert the same, to pin the shared-promise property.
3. Basis-check consequence: a kb_capture scoped to pathB citing a file that exists ONLY under pathB succeeds, and one citing a file that exists only under pathA is rejected -- proving the basis was anchored at pathB and not at whichever repo created the provider first.
4. resetKbProviders() clears the composite-keyed cache (a call after reset rebuilds rather than serving a stale anchor).
acceptance_criteria:
1. The new test file fails on the pre-fix tree (cases 1 and 3) and passes after apra-fleet-b4g.2.1.
2. Case 2 explicitly covers the concurrent unawaited path, not just sequential calls.
3. Fixtures are tmpdir-only, with a per-test unique remote so the shared FLEET_DIR sqlite files cannot bleed entries between tests.
4. npx vitest run tests/knowledge passes in full, and npm test shows no new failures elsewhere.
5. No production source file is edited by this task.
close_reason: Added tests/knowledge/kb-provider-cache-key.test.ts (4 cases): same-slug/different-repoPath anchoring, identical-pair sharing (sequential + concurrent unawaited), capture basis-check consequence, resetKbProviders() clearing the composite key. Mutation-verified: cases 1 and 3 fail when the provider cache key is reverted to slug-only. npm run build and full tests/knowledge suite (530 tests) pass. No production source file touched.

title: [test] Remote path plus remote URL resolves to the repo real KB, not the default slug
description:
File: tests/knowledge/kb-remote-scope.test.ts (new), vitest, following the fixture style of tests/knowledge/kb-repo-isolation.test.ts (makeRepo helper with git init + git remote add + a real source file for the capture basis, resetKbProviders() in beforeEach, per-test unique remote so slugs cannot collide).

Cover, in this order:
1. resolveProjectSlug unit: a Windows-style path that does not exist on this host plus git@github.com:Apra-Labs/apra-fleet.git returns githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet. Assert the negative explicitly too: the same path with NO url returns 'default'. This second assertion is the one that fails on main and is the regression pin. It satisfies parent apra-fleet-b4g.1 AC3.
2. Same assertion for the https form of the URL (both slugify to the same value).
3. Provider level: getKbProviders(<nonexistent remote path>, <fixture repo url>) and getKbProviders(<local fixture clone>) return the same projectSlug and the same dbPath.
4. Tool level, end to end: stand in for a remote member work folder with a REAL tmpdir directory that has no git origin remote of its own but does contain a real source file, and pass its path as repo_path together with repo_remote_url. kb_capture citing that file succeeds, and kb_list called with the SAME two inputs reads the entry back, while a kb_list scoped to the same repo_path with NO repo_remote_url does not see it.
   IMPORTANT -- do NOT write case 4 with a nonexistent repo_path. sqlite-provider.ts:323 rejects any capture whose cited source files do not resolve under the provider repoPath, so a nonexistent path can never round trip, before or after this sprint's fixes; the earlier draft of this case was unsatisfiable for that reason. The nonexistent-path assertion lives at the slug/provider level in cases 1-3 and in apra-fleet-b4g.1.6 case 4.
   Also give case 4 its OWN unique remote URL (or call resetKbProviders() first), so it does not inherit the provider that case 3 cached under a shared slug and anchored at a different path.
5. Backward compatibility: a local-only call with no repo_remote_url still resolves via local derivation.

kb_list only honours repo_remote_url once apra-fleet-b4g.1.4 wires it, which is why this task is blocked on it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The new test file fails on the pre-fix tree (at least the negative slug assertion in case 1 and the kb_list read-back in case 4) and passes after apra-fleet-b4g.1.1 through apra-fleet-b4g.1.4.
2. Case 4 uses a real tmpdir path with a real cited source file and asserts BOTH the positive read-back (same repo_path + repo_remote_url) and the negative (same repo_path, no URL, entry not visible).
3. The tests use only tmpdir fixtures and the suite-wide isolated APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR -- no dependency on this checkout, on FLEET_DIR state left by other tests, or on network. Each case uses a unique remote URL so slugs and sqlite files cannot bleed between cases.
4. npx vitest run tests/knowledge passes in full, with no test skipped by this change.
5. No production source file is edited by this task; if a test cannot be written without a source change, stop and report rather than widening scope.
close_reason: Added tests/knowledge/kb-remote-scope.test.ts covering AC1-5; verified fail-pre-fix/pass-post-fix on a throwaway worktree at f4b1be80, and full tests/knowledge suite (536 tests, 52 files) passes.

title: Key the KB provider cache by repo path, not slug alone
description: getKbProviders (src/services/knowledge/kb-providers.ts:73-83) caches providers in a Map keyed ONLY by project slug, while createKbProvidersForSlug(slug, cwd ?? process.cwd()) bakes a repoPath into the provider it builds. So the FIRST caller to create a given slug's provider fixes repoPath for every later caller that resolves to the same slug. Combined with the 'default' slug collapse (apra-fleet-b4g.1), every remote member shares one provider anchored at whatever directory happened to create it first -- in practice the fleet server's own cwd. Verified 2026-08-14: a kb_capture scoped to C:\Users\Kashyap\bkp\source\repos\apra-fleet was basis-checked against /home/kashyap and rejected with 'source file(s) do not exist in /home/kashyap'. Rejection is the SAFE outcome; the unsafe one is a capture citing a path that happens to exist under that unrelated directory, which would be ACCEPTED and stored with a per-file hash basis computed from a tree it does not describe -- silent corruption of the freshness basis rather than a clean failure. repoPath is load-bearing for the capture basis check and the freshness sweep (sqlite-provider.ts:275-314), so it cannot be allowed to drift from the repo the call is about.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Two getKbProviders calls with the same resolved slug but different repoPath return providers whose repoPath differs and matches what was requested. 2. A capture scoped to repo A is never basis-checked against repo B or against the server's process.cwd(). 3. A regression test covers the same-slug/different-repoPath case and fails against the current slug-only cache. 4. The concurrent-callers-share-one-provider property the current cache exists for is preserved for identical (slug, repoPath) pairs. 5. Full knowledge test suite stays green.

title: Scope the KB by git remote URL, not by a local repo path
description: resolveProjectSlug(cwd) (src/services/knowledge/project-slug.ts:4-24) shells 'git remote get-url origin' with cwd set to the caller-supplied repo_path. It already PREFERS the remote URL as the scope key -- it just cannot reach it when the directory is not on this host. For a remote member (e.g. C:\Users\Kashyap\bkp\source\repos\apra-fleet on win-apra-fleet) both git attempts fail with ENOENT and the slug degrades to the literal 'default', so every remote member on the machine pools into one empty shared database and the committed bible at <repo>/.fleet/kb-canonical.json is invisible. Verified 2026-08-14: kb_stats via that Windows path returned 0 entries / bible.present=false vs 35 entries for the same repo via its local clone. execute-prompt.ts:1372-1378 already documents this as a known, deliberate degradation 'until they get their own routing'. Fix direction: let the caller supply the repo's git remote URL (the value slugify already wants) so scope is location-independent, keeping the existing local-path derivation as the fallback.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A kb_* call scoped to a remote member's work folder resolves to the SAME project KB as the local clone of that repo, given the repo's git remote URL. 2. Existing local-member behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged when no URL is supplied (local path derivation still wins/works). 3. A regression test asserts a non-existent Windows-style path plus the apra-fleet remote URL resolves to slug githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet, not 'default'. 4. Full knowledge test suite stays green (480 tests at time of filing).

title: Make the KB correct for remote members
description: The KB is scoped and basis-checked against paths that only exist on the fleet server host. For a remote member the work folder is a path on the far side of an SSH connection, so every kb_* call scoped to it silently resolves to the wrong database. Proven empirically on member win-apra-fleet (2026-08-14), whose work folder is a clone of this repo: kb_stats via its Windows path returned 0 entries and bible.present=false, where the correct answer is 35 entries with the bible present. Local members are unaffected. Two independent defects, one child each.

title: [test] Remote-member harvest writes to that member's repo KB, not the 'default' KB
description:
[test] Prove that a remote member's auto-harvest lands in that member's repo KB and
not FLEET_DIR/knowledge/default/kb.sqlite.

WHAT TO TEST
Extend tests/execute-prompt-kb-harvest-repo-path.test.ts (vitest). Today it only
asserts the ARGUMENT handed to kbHarvest; for the remote case it never checks which
database actually receives the entry -- that gap is why this defect survived tm7.

- Set up two fake REMOTE members whose workFolders point at two different repos
  (two git repos with distinct `origin` remotes), in ONE process.
- Drive the execute_prompt auto-harvest path for each.
- Assert on the DESTINATION: the two harvested entries land in two DIFFERENT
  kb.sqlite files under FLEET_DIR/knowledge/<slug>/, and neither slug is 'default'.
- Assert the local-member case still routes by resolvedWorkFolder (existing
  assertions must keep passing, not be weakened).
- Add a negative assertion: FLEET_DIR/knowledge/default/kb.sqlite either does not
  exist or contains zero entries from this test.

HOW TO ASSERT PASS/FAIL
Point FLEET_DIR at a tmp dir per test; open the resulting sqlite files and count
rows, mirroring the style already used in tests/knowledge/kb-repo-isolation.test.ts.

DONE CRITERIA
- `npx vitest run tests/execute-prompt-kb-harvest-repo-path.test.ts` passes with
  the impl from apra-fleet-tm7.9.1 applied.
- The new destination assertions FAIL if apra-fleet-tm7.9.1's change is reverted
  (state in the task notes/PR how this was confirmed) -- a test that passes both
  before and after does not close this task.
- No test writes outside its tmp FLEET_DIR.

title: Final Review gets no KB promotion candidates, stranding late-sprint knowledge
description:
The Final Review dispatch -- the one review that sees the WHOLE sprint -- receives no KB promotion candidates,
so it can never promote anything.

OBSERVED 2026-08-10, sprint feat/zone-transit-engine. Its final reviewer reported verbatim:

  "No Knowledge Bank tools were available in this session and the dispatch prompt carried no
   promotion-candidate block, so there is nothing to promote."

Meanwhile the SAME sprint's per-round reviewers promoted 3 entries, and the concurrent BFF sprint promoted 15,
all with zero rejections -- so the apra-fleet-0ef fix works on the path it covers.

ROOT CAUSE: kbCandidates is threaded only through buildReviewerPrompt (runner.js ~3823) and its single caller
dispatchReview (~5735, which calls kbWork.promotionCandidates then passes kbCandidates at ~5776). The Final
Review builds its prompt with buildFinalVerdictPrompt (~4119), which has no kbCandidates parameter and no
promotionCandidates call anywhere near it. So 0ef was fixed for per-round review and re-review only.

WHY IT MATTERS: the final reviewer is the best-positioned promoter in the whole run. It has read the entire
diff, run the full suite, and judged the sprint as a whole -- exactly the evidence standard reviewer.md demands
before minting CONFIRMED. Every entry a doer captured in the last round of a sprint reaches this reviewer and
nobody else, so late-sprint knowledge is systematically stranded at INFERRED.

FIX: same shape as dispatchReview -- fetch promotionCandidates(reviewerRepoPath) before the final-review
dispatch, render the same "KNOWLEDGE BANK -- promotion candidates" block into buildFinalVerdictPrompt, and run
the returned kb_promotions through kbWork.apply. The final-verdict output schema needs the kb_promotions field
too if it does not carry one.

DONE = a final review can promote; a sprint whose last round captures a verified fact ends with that fact
CONFIRMED rather than INFERRED.
close_reason: Fixed in fc039401. buildFinalVerdictPrompt now takes kbCandidates and renders the promotion block; finalVerdict gained kb_promotions; the final review fetches candidates once before dispatch (so retry/resume reuse the same block) and runs the result through kbWork.apply, ungated by verdict. The block itself is now kbPromotionBlock(), shared verbatim by both reviewer prompts so their evidence bars cannot drift. 5 new tests in packages/apra-fleet-se/test/final-review-kb-promotion.test.mjs, verified RED without the fix (import of kbPromotionBlock fails). Golden transcript regenerated; sole change is the kb_promotions schema property, prompt body byte-identical. apra-fleet-se 2103/0.

title: kb_stats reports zeros for a repo where kb_list returns 38 entries
description:
kb_stats reports all-zero totals for a repo whose KB demonstrably holds entries.

OBSERVED 2026-08-10, both repos, immediately after two sprints that promoted 18 entries with zero rejections:

  kb_stats  repo_path=/home/kashyap/repos/apra/apra-warehouse-analytics
    -> {"totals":{"by_confidence":{"CONFIRMED":0,"INFERRED":0,"UNVERIFIED":0},...,"total":0},
        "promote_ratio":null,"bible":{"present":false,"entries":0}}

  kb_list   repo_path=<same path>  confidence=CONFIRMED  -> 28 results
  kb_list   repo_path=<same path>  confidence=INFERRED   -> 10 results

Same for /home/kashyap/repos/apra/apra-analytics: kb_stats total 0, kb_list returns 3 CONFIRMED + 3 INFERRED.
Identical repo_path string in both calls, same MCP session, same server (v0.4.0_c2381c).

IMPACT: kb_stats is the natural way an operator or an agent asks "is the KB working here?", and it currently
answers "there is nothing here" for a healthy, populated KB. That is worse than an error: during the 0ef
investigation this reading would have supported the wrong conclusion (that promotion never happens), when in
fact promotion was working. promote_ratio is null for the same reason, so the one metric that would show the
capture->promote funnel is also dead.

Note bible.present=false while entries exist, which suggests kb_stats may be reading a different store or a
different scoping key than kb_list (canonical/bible export vs live DB), rather than mis-counting.

DONE = kb_stats and kb_list agree on the same repo_path, and promote_ratio reflects real capture/promote counts.
close_reason: Fixed in fc039401. CORRECTION to this bead's own diagnosis: the cause was not a different store or scoping key -- kb_stats declares its input as `repo`, while kb_list/kb_capture/kb_promote/kb_session_prime/kb_export all declare `repo_path`. I called it with repo_path, zod stripped the unknown key silently, and it fell back to the fleet server's cwd. Verified live: kb_stats {repo: <warehouse>} returns CONFIRMED 28 / INFERRED 10 / total 41 / promote_ratio 1, while {repo_path: <same>} returns all zeros. kb_stats now accepts repo_path as an alias (repo wins if both given, so no existing caller changes). 3 new tests in tests/knowledge/kb-stats.test.ts; 17/17 there, 467/467 root vitest.

title: A parent bead whose children all closed is undispatchable but still counts against the completion gate, stalling the sprint
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-07, sprint feat/forklift-stationary-handling (scope --parent apra-warehouse-analytics-onk). All 13 task beads closed and 15 commits landed with a green suite (124/124), but the sprint still died:

  StalledSprintError: 2 consecutive cycle(s) made no new high-water-mark progress.
  Closed-count history: [9, 14, 14, 14] (high-water 14).

ROOT CAUSE -- two sites disagree about whether a parent bead is work:

1. readyBeads (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, the parentIds filter) deliberately EXCLUDES any bead that is some other bead's parent, so a parent is never dispatched to a doer. This is correct and intentional (apra-fleet-eft 15 C2: doers correctly refuse non-task parents, wasting a dispatch each).

2. openAtGoal (runner.js, the bdListScoped call using --status plus --priority-max plus --json) applies NO parent filter. Every open parent at or above goal priority counts toward the completion gate.

So a parent whose children have all closed is simultaneously (a) impossible to dispatch and (b) permanently blocking. openAtGoal can never reach 0, therefore:
- the completion gate (openAtGoal.length === 0 AND lastReviewVerdict === APPROVED) can never fire;
- the re-review branch guarded by the same openAtGoal.length === 0 condition (apra-fleet-s6d) is likewise unreachable;
- the run burns cycles until the stall guard aborts it, discarding the harvest and PR phases even though every task succeeded.

In this run the three blockers were the epic (onk) and the two bug parents (awt, u98). Closing them by hand afterwards left a clean board, which confirms the diagnosis.

This is NOT the same defect as apra-fleet-s6d. s6d is about the re-review PROMPT being incoherent once that branch is entered; this is about the branch (and the exit gate) being unreachable in the first place. Fixing s6d alone leaves this untouched.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) apply the same parentIds exclusion to openAtGoal so the gate counts only dispatchable work; (b) auto-close a parent when its last child closes; or (c) keep counting parents but treat all-children-closed as satisfied. Option (a) is the smallest and most consistent with readyBeads. Whichever is chosen, the stall-abort message should name WHICH beads are blocking -- the current message reports only counts, so an operator cannot see that the blockers are undispatchable parents.

Also worth noting: the user's original report of the s6d Re-Review defect was triggered by mid-sprint bead closing, which is precisely the manual workaround this bug forces.
close_reason:
Fixed via option (a) -- the completion gate now counts only DISPATCHABLE work -- plus the diagnostic half of the bead.

CHANGE (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js):
- New decomposedParentIds(): single source of truth for "this bead is a grouping node, not a unit of work". Built from bdListScoped('') so it issues no new bd command, and from children of ANY status so an all-children-closed parent does not stop looking like a parent.
- readyLeafBeads() now consumes it (was an inline duplicate of the same expression) -- the two sites can no longer drift, which was the whole defect.
- The per-cycle openAtGoal and the final finalOpenAtGoal both filter it out.
- errors.mjs: StalledSprintError gained a blockerIds field.
- The stall-abort message now names the beads still open at/above goal priority, or states explicitly that none are (i.e. the stall is in closing out the sprint, not in the work).

Deliberately NOT done: auto-closing the parent (option b). The gate ignores it; who closes it stays a separate, explicit decision. A test pins that it remains open.

EVIDENCE:
- New regression test packages/apra-fleet-se/test/mock-sprint-parent-gate-completion.test.mjs builds the epic -> bug -> task nesting a planner produces. Pre-fix it reproduced the live failure exactly: StalledSprintError, closed-count history [2, 2, 2], staleCycles 2, and a message naming no blockers. Post-fix the same scenario reaches Final Review -> Harvest -> Publish PR in cycle 1 -- the three phases the 2026-08-07 run lost.
- The sprint epic itself never reproduced this: a target WITH children is excluded from scopeIds, so it is invisible to every scoped query. Only a parent NESTED under the target hits both sides of the contradiction.
- mock-sprint-stall-zero-progress.test.mjs extended to assert blockerIds is populated and that every id appears in the abort message.
- Full apra-fleet-se suite: 1136 tests, 0 fail. Golden transcript unchanged (no prompt drift).

Not yet committed; the change sits on branch fix/kb-promote-and-rereview alongside the 0ef/s6d fix.

title: kb_promote can never fire: reviewer is never given candidate entry ids, and kb_promote is called without repo_path
description:
Across ~10 capture rounds in two dubai-warehouse sprints, kb_promote succeeded zero times; every entry sits at INFERRED. The provider's conservative gates are NOT the cause -- they are never reached. The sprint logs contain zero '[kb-work] promote <id>', zero 'kb_promote rejected' and zero 'refused' lines; only '[kb-work] reviewer: captured N, promoted 0'.

ROOT CAUSE (missing input, two contracts in conflict):
1. The engine's design (runner.js:2060-2064) is 'judgment belongs to the role, execution belongs here': the reviewer returns kb_promotions:[{id,reason}] and createKbWorkClient.apply calls kb_promote in-process.
2. kb_promotions appears NOWHERE in packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/reviewer.md. The persona's Step 5 instead instructs the reviewer to call mcp__apra-fleet__kb_list and mcp__apra-fleet__kb_promote DIRECTLY -- the pre-engine model. Persona and engine implement different contracts.
3. The reviewer subagent has no apra-fleet MCP tools. Its own sprint notes: 'ToolSearch returned no kb_* tools (apra-fleet MCP server not running)'. reviewer.md Step 5 says 'If the KB tools are unavailable, skip this step', so it skips.
4. buildReviewerPrompt (runner.js:3555-3581) injects no KB context at all, and the id field in agents/schemas/reviewer-output.json:69 carries no description of where an id comes from.

Net: the reviewer has no way to learn a single KB entry id, so kb_promotions is structurally always empty. kb_captures works precisely because a capture needs no pre-existing id.

LATENT SECOND BUG (blocks the fix): runner.js:2192 calls kb_promote WITHOUT repo_path, while kb_capture at runner.js:2176 passes it. Per src/tools/kb-promote.ts:6 a server-handled call without repo_path resolves against the fleet server cwd -- the wrong KB -- so every promotion would fail 'Entry not found' even once ids are supplied. Same class as apra-fleet-tm7, fixed for capture but never for promote.

FIX (decided with user 2026-08-07): engine-injects-candidates.
(a) Engine calls kb_list(confidence INFERRED, repo_path) before the review dispatch and embeds id/title/summary/source_files in the reviewer prompt.
(b) Pass repo_path on the kb_promote call at runner.js:2192.
(c) Rewrite reviewer.md Step 5 to the engine contract: read candidates from the prompt, return kb_promotions, do not call MCP kb tools.
(d) Describe the id field in reviewer-output.json.

title: Re-Review dispatches the reviewer with zero bead ids, then aborts the sprint on its honest refusal
description:
Cycle Evaluation's re-review path calls dispatchReview({beadIds: [], ...}) at packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:7795. buildReviewerPrompt (runner.js:3557) renders that as the literal sentence 'Review the work just done for the following bead id(s): .' -- naming nothing -- and the SPRINT SCOPE block (runner.js:3568) then tells the reviewer to 'Judge your verdict ONLY against the named bead id(s) above', i.e. against an empty set. The resume prompt (runner.js:5265) has the same empty join.

The reviewer correctly answers that there is nothing to act on: CHANGES_NEEDED with empty reopenIds and empty newTasks. isReviewerContractViolation (runner.js:3593) classifies that as a contract violation, dispatchReview retries with the IDENTICAL incoherent prompt, gets the identical answer, and throws ReviewerContractViolationError (runner.js:5385), aborting the sprint.

The re-review is legitimately a SCOPE-WIDE question ('is the sprint actually done?'), but it is forced through a prompt builder whose contract is per-bead. Empty beadIds is a valid state for this one call site and neither the prompt builder nor the contract check knows it.

Fix: give buildReviewerPrompt a scope-wide framing when beadIds is empty (point the reviewer at the bdListScoped JSON already passed as acceptanceCriteriaJson) so the dispatch is coherent. Same for the resume prompt. Observed live in the dubai-warehouse forklift sprints.

title: [bug] kb_capture reports success but writes nothing: 3 captures lost, no store gained rows
description:
fleet-sprint's reviewer logged:
  [kb-work] reviewer: captured 3, promoted 0
during Review C2 R1 of a live sprint on member 'local-warehouse-analytics'
(repo /home/kashyap/repos/apra/apra-warehouse-analytics), fleet v0.4.0_a3e4a8.

createKbWorkClient.apply() only increments `captured` when callTool('kb_capture', ...)
returns without throwing (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js ~2151), so
three capture calls were accepted. Nothing was persisted.

EVIDENCE
 - ~/.apra-fleet/data/knowledge/githubcom-apra-labs-apra-warehouse-analytics/:
     entries=0, links=0
     kb.sqlite      mtime 17:26:41  (pre-fix)
     kb.sqlite-wal  mtime 17:26:42  (pre-fix -- NOT written during the sprint)
     kb.sqlite-shm  mtime 19:25:28  (priming opened the DB to read; read-only)
 - No other store gained rows: default=0, githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet=23
   (unchanged), global=0. No new store directory was created.

NOT the capture-vs-promote distinction. src/tools/kb-capture.ts writes captures at
INFERRED confidence and documents kb_promote as 'the ONLY path that mints CONFIRMED',
so promoted=0 should still leave 3 INFERRED rows behind. It left none.

The sprint-engine call site looks correct -- kb_capture is invoked with
repo_path: repoPath, and repoPath was non-null (kb-prime resolved it this run, see
apra-fleet-n78). So the loss is downstream of the engine. Two candidates:
 1. getKbProviders(input.repo_path) resolving to a provider that silently discards.
 2. kb_capture returning an MCP isError result instead of throwing -- callTool would
    not throw, so captured++ counts a write that never happened. If so, the engine
    should also treat an isError result as a failure rather than success.

IMPACT: sprints appear to accumulate knowledge and do not. The reviewer's captured
findings are silently discarded, so the KB stays empty no matter how many sprints run
-- which is why the warehouse store still had entries=0 after a full cycle.

Related: apra-fleet-n78 (kb-prime folder resolution, fixed), apra-fleet-tm7 /
apra-fleet-tm7.9 (kb_harvest repo-blindness) -- same subsystem, different call sites.

REPRO: run fleet-sprint to a Review phase and diff entry counts across
~/.apra-fleet/data/knowledge/*/kb.sqlite before and after.
notes:
ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE (same sprint, Harvest C5, fleet v0.4.0_a3e4a8):

The harvester returned:
  'KNOWLEDGE BANK: ToolSearch returned no kb_* tools (apra-fleet MCP server not
   running), so Step 0 priming and Step 5 CONFIRMED promotion were both skipped.
   Nothing was promoted; no beads were mutated.'

The agent's parenthetical is WRONG and worth not taking at face value: the server
was running throughout (apra-fleet status -> running, pid 104931, v0.4.0_a3e4a8),
and 'claude mcp list' from the member's work folder reports
  apra-fleet: http://localhost:7523/mcp (HTTP) - Connected
So the server was up and reachable from the member. The kb_* tools were simply not
discoverable via the dispatched agent's ToolSearch.

Post-harvest store counts, unchanged from before the sprint:
  default=0, githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet=23, warehouse-analytics=0, global=0

So BOTH KB write paths failed in one run, with different symptoms:
 - reviewer captures: orchestrator-side callTool('kb_capture') reported success,
   nothing persisted (the original report above).
 - harvester promotion: agent-side, kb_* tools never surfaced to the agent at all,
   so the step was skipped and self-reported as 'server not running'.

Whether these share a root cause (kb_* tools not actually registered/exposed by
this build) or are two separate defects is the first thing to determine. If the
tools are genuinely unregistered, that would also explain the orchestrator's
phantom success: an unknown-tool MCP error result that callTool does not throw on,
so captured++ counts a write that never happened.

NEXT STEP: enumerate the server's tools/list (needs an mcp-session-id handshake;
a bare POST returns 'Missing mcp-session-id header') and confirm whether kb_capture
/ kb_promote / kb_session_prime are registered at all.

title: [bug] kb-prime never primes any member: member_detail called without format:'json'
description:
createKbPrimingClient.folderFor (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:2004) calls:
  callTool('member_detail', { member_name: member })

member_detail's format param defaults to 'compact' (src/tools/member-detail.ts:17). Two consequences:
 1. parseResult() JSON.parse()s the compact text -> throws -> returns null.
 2. The compact renderer never emits the work folder at all; `folder: agent.workFolder` is only set on the json path (member-detail.ts:41).

So folderFor() returns null for EVERY member, primeAll() logs
  [kb-prime] no work folder for member '<m>' -- skipping (KB stays cold)
and the KB is never populated for any sprint.

EVIDENCE (live fleet-sprint run 2026-08-06, member local-warehouse-analytics):
  log line emitted as above; the per-repo store
  ~/.apra-fleet/data/knowledge/githubcom-apra-labs-apra-warehouse-analytics/kb.sqlite
  was created (schema only) with entries=0, links=0.

This defeats the repo-scoping the surrounding comment says it exists to provide.
FIX: pass { member_name: member, format: 'json' }.
Related: apra-fleet-tm7 (kb_harvest repo-blindness) -- same class of defect, different call site.

title: Phase 3: rebuild the bible
description: Only after Phases 0-2. Step 1 mechanical triage of all 97 entries offline against the current tree (delegatable, fully checkable). Steps 2-3 are judgment and must NOT be blindly delegated: verification gate via kb_promote with recorded reasons, then gap-fill for what the refactor created. Step 4 a single kb_export with autoCommit false, then a deliberate reviewed commit.
acceptance_criteria: Every surviving entry earns CONFIRMED through kb_promote with a recorded reason under the Phase 1 invariants. Final kb-canonical.json diff read by a human before commit.
close_reason: Bible rebuilt 97 -> 17 (2a66936). Scripted triage (58 candidate / 6 repointable / 33 droppable), then a by-hand verification gate: promoted only claims read and confirmed in the current source. All 17 earned CONFIRMED via kb_promote and carry their evidence in-KB. Found two mutually contradictory CONFIRMED pairs (9462ab04 vs c5f1f415; 4cdf2a5d vs f782fa69), both settled against the source. 80 drops recorded in docs/kb-bible-rebuild-2026-08-04.md; unverified code-intelligence entries were dropped rather than re-blessed on trust.

title: Phase 3a: bible records its export commit (v2 format, dual-shape import)
description: kb_export writes a bare JSON array (kb-export.ts:198); kb_import throws on anything else (kb-import.ts:121-122). New shape: {version:2, provenance:{commit,branch,entry_count}, entries:[...]}. Record the commit, not a timestamp -- a timestamp would defeat the sorted-by-id 'meaningful diffs' property (kb-export.ts:178). Resolve via git rev-parse HEAD in repoPath, writing null rather than throwing when unavailable. IMPORT SIDE MUST SHIP BEFORE OR WITH EXPORT SIDE, never after.
acceptance_criteria: A legacy bare-array bible and a v2 object bible import identically. A v2 export followed by a v2 import preserves the entry set. Two exports at the same commit with the same entries are byte-identical.
close_reason: v2 bible format landed in 629ea1b. kb_import accepts both shapes (verified legacy bare-array still imports BEFORE the export side wrote v2). kb_export writes {version,provenance:{commit,branch,entry_count},entries}. Two exports at the same commit are byte-identical; an unchanged entry set rewrites nothing, which also fixes a self-perturbing loop where auto-commit moved HEAD and every export re-committed. kb_stats (the third bible reader) also handles both shapes -- it degraded silently before. 12 tests, 7 of which fail without the change.

title: Phase 2: engine-executed KB capture and promote
description: Split plumbing from judgment. Engines call kb_session_prime/kb_import/kb_export/kb_list directly via the injected callTool (as member_reservation already does at runner.js:1798), replacing primeKB()'s Haiku dispatch (auto-sprint.js:1652) and giving fleet-sprint/runner.js the KB priming it lacks (apra-fleet-e28). Roles return decisions in structured output; the engine makes the calls. kb_promotions stays reviewer-only.
acceptance_criteria: A schema payload results in the corresponding tool call; a malformed or unverifiable payload results in no call; a kb_promotions payload from a non-reviewer role is rejected.
notes: auto-sprint half landed in 00e1acb: schemas (incl. new planner-output.json), engine-side vetKbWork validation + logging, executor-agent dispatch, kb_promotions reviewer-only, 14 unit tests. RUNNER.JS HALF BLOCKED: runner.js has no repo-path concept in its ALLOWED args, in bin/cli.mjs, or anywhere in the file -- it coordinates members by name and branch, and the repo lives on each member's (possibly remote) side. kb_session_prime needs repo_path; omitting it falls back to the fleet server cwd, which is exactly the apra-fleet-tm7 repo-blindness defect. Needs a decision on where the path comes from before apra-fleet-e28 can close.
close_reason: Both halves landed. auto-sprint (00e1acb): schemas incl. new planner-output.json, engine-side vetKbWork validation + logging, executor-agent dispatch, planner converted to structured output. fleet-sprint (2820749): per-member KB priming via member_detail work folders, and direct callTool kb_capture/kb_promote consumption of the shared schema fields. kb_promotions reviewer-only in both engines. 37 new tests (14 apra-pm + 23 apra-fleet-se). Suites: root 3363/0, apra-fleet-se 942/0, apra-pm 436/1 (pre-existing cycle-checkpoint).

title: Phase 1: push KB capture/promote invariants into SqliteProvider.capture()
description: Four call sites reach provider.capture() independently (kb-capture.ts:122, kb-harvest.ts:134, kb-import.ts:172, kb-server.ts:139), so tool-layer enforcement is bypassed by three of four. Follows the D1 clamp precedent at sqlite-provider.ts:666-671. Invariants: reject zero source_files; reject non-existent source_files (no importMode exemption); kb_promote requires a non-trivial reason; kb_promote refuses entries whose source_files no longer resolve; kb_export defaults bible.autoCommit to false. Harvest batches must isolate rejections and report entries_rejected.
acceptance_criteria: Each invariant has a test that fails without the fix and passes with it. Rejection asserted through all four call sites, not just kb_capture. Batch-isolation test: one rejectable + one valid entry stores the valid one and reports entries_rejected: 1.
close_reason: All five invariants enforced in SqliteProvider.capture()/promote(): zero source_files rejected (user-directive exempt), non-existent source_files rejected, promote requires a >=20-char evidence reason, promote refuses an unresolvable basis, kb_export autoCommit defaults false. Rejection asserted through all four call sites plus the provider directly. Batch isolation via entries_rejected (harvest) and rejected (import). Commits 317e1b1, 9aa06c0. Full suite 251 files / 3363 tests, 0 failures.

Four strictly ordered phases: 0 restore executing contracts, 1 provider-level invariants, 2 engine-executed capture/promote, 3 rebuild the bible (with 3a bible provenance). Phases are strictly ordered; Phase 3 does not start until 0-2 are done.

Phase 0 (3a31699, 7eb944f), Phase 1 (317e1b1, 9aa06c0, d944c3f), Phase 2 (00e1acb, 2820749), Phase 3a (629ea1b), Phase 3 (2a66936), plus the follow-ups 4wz.7/8/9 and a Phase 1 regression fixed in 6d52ad5. title: Remote-member auto-harvest routes to that member's repo KB, not the shared 'default' KB
description:
Remote-member auto-harvest still violates tm7's per-repo isolation intent for the
fleet's primary deployment shape (remote members).

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR (verified at HEAD)
- src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:1368-1390 always passes `resolvedWorkFolder` as
  `repo_path` to kbHarvest, for local AND remote members (the tm7.2 comment says

title: kb_harvest still repo-blind after 3zl: auto-harvest routes via a second singleton (getKBService) bound to server cwd
description:
kb_harvest -- the highest-volume KB writer, auto-fired after EVERY
execute_prompt -- is still repo-blind after the apra-fleet-3zl fix. It reaches
the database through a SECOND memoised singleton that 3zl did not touch.

THE CHAIN (all verified)
  src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:796  auto-harvest fires after every prompt,
                                   passing only { session_transcript, session_id }
                                   -- no repo, no member, no cwd
  src/tools/kb-harvest.ts:102      const service = getKBService();
  src/services/knowledge/kb-service.ts:49
                                   getKBService() memoises _instance globally;
                                   no repo parameter exists at all
  kb-service.ts:38                 new SqliteProvider(config?.dbPath) -- dbPath
                                   is undefined
  sqlite-provider.ts:59            dbPath undefined -> resolveProjectSlug() with
                                   NO argument -> process.cwd()

process.cwd() in the fleet server is wherever the server was started. So every
harvest, from every member, working in every repo, lands in that one KB.

WHY 3zl's FIX DID NOT COVER IT
3zl threaded repo_path into getKbProviders() and made that cache per-slug. Its
done criterion -- "no kb_* tool calls getKbProviders() with no argument" -- was
met and is still true. kb_harvest simply never called getKbProviders; it uses
getKBService, a parallel path with its own singleton. The criterion was
satisfied while the intent (per-repo isolation) was not. My mistake in scoping
3zl: I audited call sites of one accessor instead of auditing every route to a
provider.

OBSERVED
During the apra-fleet-7um reviewer proof, the reviewer ran entirely in a scratch
clone (slug exampleinvalid-kb-reviewer-proof) and its kb_list/kb_promote calls
correctly hit the scratch KB. But the post-dispatch auto-harvest opened
data/knowledge/githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet/kb.sqlite -- the server's cwd
repo, unrelated to the dispatch. It wrote 0 entries that run (nothing worth
harvesting), so no data crossed over, but the write path is plainly bound to
the wrong repo.

IMPACT
Harvest is the ONLY fully automatic KB writer. Everything else is called
deliberately by an agent with a repo_path. So in normal fleet operation the
automatic path is exactly the one that ignores which repo the work happened in:
a doer's session learnings on repo B are harvested into repo A's KB, then
served to repo A's future sessions by kb_session_prime as if local.

FIX SKETCH
- execute_prompt must pass the member's working folder to kbHarvest; it knows
  it (the member record carries workFolder).
- kb_harvest takes repo_path like every other kb_* tool.
- getKBService needs per-repo keying, or kb_harvest should route through
  getKbProviders like its siblings. Prefer the latter -- two parallel provider
  accessors with different caching is the root defect, not a detail.
- Audit for any OTHER route to a provider: src/index.ts:140 also calls
  getKBService(), as does the kb-server command path.

Done criteria:
- A harvest triggered by a prompt on a member working in repo B writes to repo
  B's KB, proven by test with two repos in one process
- No provider is reachable by a code path that resolves its repo from
  process.cwd() when a caller-supplied repo is available

title: All KB tools resolve the database from server cwd and memoise it -- every repo's knowledge collapses into one KB
description:
Every KB tool resolves its database from the SERVER PROCESS's cwd, not from
the repo the call is about, and the resolution is memoised process-wide. In a
long-running fleet server this collapses every member's knowledge into one
KB -- whichever repo the server happened to start in.

TWO DEFECTS THAT COMPOUND

1. repo_path is accepted but never used to select the provider.
   Audited all 16 src/tools/kb-*.ts: NOT ONE passes an argument to
   getKbProviders(). kb_export, kb_session_prime and kb_setup take a
   repo_path/repo param and use it for FILE paths (where to write the bible,
   where to install the hook) but not for choosing the database.

     src/tools/kb-capture.ts:49   const providers = await getKbProviders();

   getKbProviders(cwd?) -> createKbProviders(cwd) -> resolveProjectSlug(cwd
   ?? process.cwd()). With no argument the slug always comes from the calling
   PROCESS's cwd.

2. The provider is a memoised singleton.
   src/services/knowledge/kb-providers.ts:28

     export async function getKbProviders(cwd?) {
       if (!_providers) { _providers = await createKbProviders(cwd); }
       return _providers;
     }

   The FIRST kb_* call in the process fixes the KB for that process's entire
   lifetime. Even if a later call passed a cwd, it would be ignored.

CONSEQUENCE IN THE SHIPPED TOPOLOGY
The HTTP fleet server is long-lived and serves every member. This machine has
13 members registered across 8 distinct repos. Every kb_capture, kb_promote,
kb_query and kb_session_prime from any of them lands in ONE database, chosen
by wherever the server was started. Per-repo knowledge isolation -- which the
directory layout (data/knowledge/<project-slug>/kb.sqlite) plainly intends --
does not hold at runtime.

Worse, kb_export composes the two halves incorrectly: it reads entries from
the cwd-resolved KB but writes the bible to repo_path/.fleet/. So exporting
"for" repo B can serialise repo A's knowledge into repo B's committed,
git-shared bible. Cross-project leakage into a reviewed artifact.

HOW IT WAS FOUND
Seeding a scratch KB for the apra-fleet-7um reviewer proof: the script ran
with cwd = the real repo but passed repo_path = a scratch clone. All three
entries landed in the REAL project KB (githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet),
not the scratch slug. Removed; the real KB was cold beforehand so nothing was
lost.

INTERACTION WITH OTHER BEADS
- apra-fleet-k5j (HTTPS remotes slug to the directory basename) makes this
  worse: two repos can collide on slug even when resolution is per-call.
- apra-fleet-7um dispatches reviewers on members across repos. Until this is
  fixed, a reviewer promoting on one repo can write into another repo's KB.
- apra-fleet-ong (bible truncation) shares the kb_export read/write split.

FIX SKETCH
- Thread the caller's repo through: getKbProviders(repoPath) on every tool,
  with repo_path promoted from optional to required where the call is
  repo-scoped.
- Replace the single _providers slot with a Map keyed by resolved slug, so
  concurrent repos each get their own provider without re-creating per call.
- kb_export must read and write the SAME repo -- assert the source slug
  matches the destination repo before writing a bible.

Done criteria:
- A test with two distinct repo paths in ONE process proves entries written
  for repo A are invisible to repo B
- kb_export refuses, or is proven unable, to write repo A's entries into repo
  B's .fleet/
- No kb_* tool calls getKbProviders() with no argument
close_reason: Fixed in 502932e on chore/merge-main-into-code-intel. getKbProviders now caches per resolved slug (Map of promises) instead of a single slot; all 16 kb_* tools plus code_context enrichment thread the caller's repo, with the four that already resolved a path passing the RESOLVED value so kb_export's source and destination cannot diverge; the single global KB moved to its own cache. slugify's userinfo strip bounded to the authority section, so plain HTTPS no longer slugs to '' and falls back to the directory basename. tests/knowledge/kb-repo-isolation.test.ts (8 cases) verified as a genuine regression test -- 5 fail against pre-fix code. Build exit 0; 244 files / 3285 tests pass.

comments.author: kashhash
comments.text: SCOPE CORRECTION: this fix is real but NARROWER than its close reason implies. It covered every route through getKbProviders(). It did NOT cover kb_harvest, which reaches a provider via a second, independent memoised singleton -- getKBService() -> new SqliteProvider(undefined) -> resolveProjectSlug() with no argument -> process.cwd(). Since auto-harvest fires after EVERY execute_prompt, that is the highest-volume KB write path in normal fleet operation, and it remains bound to the server's cwd. Filed as apra-fleet-tm7. My scoping error: I audited call sites of one accessor rather than every route to a provider.

title: resolveProjectSlug maps every HTTPS remote to empty -- KBs namespaced by directory name, projects can collide
description:
resolveProjectSlug() maps every HTTPS git remote to an empty slug, silently
falling back to the repo's DIRECTORY BASENAME to namespace the project KB.
Two unrelated projects checked out into same-named directories therefore
SHARE one knowledge bank.

Root cause -- src/services/knowledge/project-slug.ts:29

    .replace(/^https?:\/\/[^@]*@?/, '')

The intent is "strip optional userinfo after the scheme". But `[^@]*` is
greedy and not bounded to the authority section, so when the URL contains no
'@' at all it consumes the ENTIRE remainder of the URL. slugify returns '',
resolveProjectSlug falls through to branch 2, and the KB is namespaced by
path.basename(repoRoot).

Verified:
  git@github.com:Apra-Labs/apra-fleet.git      -> "githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet"  (correct)
  https://user@github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet.git -> "githubcom-apra-labs-apra-fleet"  (correct)
  https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet.git  -> ""   <-- BUG
  https://gitlab.com/other/project.git         -> ""   <-- BUG

Only SSH remotes and HTTPS-with-userinfo work. Plain HTTPS is GitHub's
default clone URL, so this is the common case, not an edge case.

IMPACT
1. Cross-project KB contamination. ~/work/api and ~/personal/api both slug to
   "api" and share one kb.sqlite. One project's CONFIRMED entries prime the
   other's sessions and can be exported into the wrong repo's bible.
2. Lost continuity in the other direction. The same project cloned to
   apra-fleet/ and apra-fleet-review/ gets two disjoint KBs, so a warm session
   goes cold for no visible reason.
3. Silent. Nothing logs the fallback; the only symptom is a KB that seems to
   remember the wrong things.

This repo is not currently exposed -- its remote is SSH -- which is likely why
it has gone unnoticed.

FIX (bound the userinfo match to the authority section):

    .replace(/^https?:\/\/(?:[^@/]*@)?/, '')

Done criteria:
- All four URL forms above produce a correct, distinct slug
- Table-driven unit test in tests/knowledge/ covering ssh, https, https+userinfo,
  scp-style, and trailing-slash variants
- Decide whether existing mis-namespaced KB directories need a migration or
  can be left (they are caches, but CONFIRMED entries in a wrong-project bible
  are not purely disposable)
close_reason: Fixed in 502932e on chore/merge-main-into-code-intel. getKbProviders now caches per resolved slug (Map of promises) instead of a single slot; all 16 kb_* tools plus code_context enrichment thread the caller's repo, with the four that already resolved a path passing the RESOLVED value so kb_export's source and destination cannot diverge; the single global KB moved to its own cache. slugify's userinfo strip bounded to the authority section, so plain HTTPS no longer slugs to '' and falls back to the directory basename. tests/knowledge/kb-repo-isolation.test.ts (8 cases) verified as a genuine regression test -- 5 fail against pre-fix code. Build exit 0; 244 files / 3285 tests pass.

title: kb_export silently truncates the committed bible when cited files are absent -- and auto-commits it
description:
kb_export can silently truncate the committed team bible, and it AUTO-COMMITS
the truncation. Found while proving the bible round-trip end to end
(apra-fleet-7um), running the real built tools against an isolated scratch
repo + APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR.

REPRODUCTION (real tools, no mocks):
1. Scratch git repo containing only README.md + a copy of this repo's real
   97-entry .fleet/kb-canonical.json
2. kb_import  -> 97 entries land; the post-import freshness sweep runs
3. kb_export  -> writes 15 entries and AUTO-COMMITS
   ("chore(kb): update knowledge bible -- 15 confirmed entries")

Scratch KB state after the run: 98 total, 91 CONFIRMED, of which 76 stale=1
and only 15 stale=0. The sweep correctly staled every entry whose
source_files do not exist in that worktree; kb_export correctly emits only
CONFIRMED AND non-stale. Each step is behaving as designed. The composition
is the problem: 82 entries silently left the shared artifact and the loss was
committed without a human in the loop.

THE DB IS FINE -- stale entries are retained and revivable via
kb_freshness_sweep. The damage is to the BIBLE FILE, which is the transport
other machines import from. A truncated commit propagates the loss to
everyone who pulls.

LIVE EXPOSURE IN THIS REPO (read-only check against HEAD 2ded82b):
29 of 97 bible entries cite at least one source_file that does not exist at
HEAD. Mostly ephemeral sprint artifacts -- feedback.md, PLAN.md,
requirements.md -- plus .gitnexus/ and tests/kb-user-directive.test.ts.
So an import+export cycle in this repo today would drop the bible from 97 to
roughly 68 and commit it.

GOOD NEWS: 0 entries cite vendor/apra-pm, so the submodule-to-package move in
apra-fleet-iri stranded nothing.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW: apra-fleet-7um wires the reviewer to promote, which
increases kb_export frequency. Amplifying export without fixing this makes
truncation more likely, not less.

CANDIDATE FIXES (needs a decision):
a. Refuse to auto-commit when the export count DROPS by more than N, or by
   more than X% -- require an explicit override. Cheapest real guard.
b. Do not let entries pinned only to ephemeral sprint artifacts
   (feedback.md, PLAN.md, requirements.md) carry a hash basis at all --
   they should never have been freshness-gated.
c. Export the UNION of current CONFIRMED-non-stale and what the existing
   bible already holds, so export is additive and removal is deliberate.
d. Separate "export" from "commit" entirely; make committing a human step.

Done criteria:
- An export that would shrink the bible cannot auto-commit unnoticed
- A regression test covering the import -> sweep -> export -> commit chain in
  a worktree missing some cited files
close_reason:
Both done-criteria met, across this branch.

CRITERION 1 -- an export that would shrink the bible cannot auto-commit
unnoticed. Fix (d) was taken: separate export from commit. autoCommitEnabled()
now defaults to FALSE (kb-export.ts), so a shrinking export lands as a
reviewable working-tree diff and the committed artifact at HEAD is untouched.
Missing file, missing section and malformed JSON all degrade to false, so a
config problem cannot silently start committing on the team's behalf.

Phase 1 also changed WHERE the loss happens. Entries citing absent or no files
are now refused at the SqliteProvider.capture() choke point, so they are
counted as 'rejected' at import instead of entering the DB, being staled by the
sweep, and then quietly falling out of the export. The v2 bible envelope
additionally records provenance.entry_count, so a truncation is visible in the
diff rather than only as a shorter list.

CRITERION 2 -- regression test over the chain in a worktree missing cited
files: tests/knowledge/kb-bible-truncation-commit.test.ts (6 tests, commit
1be23cc). Real git worktree, real files, real import -> sweep -> export ->
commit. Proved load-bearing by reverting both halves of the fix (basis check
disabled, autoCommit default flipped back to true): all 6 fail.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, deliberately recorded in the test: an explicit
bible.autoCommit=true opt-in STILL commits a truncation. There is no
shrink-size guard (candidate fix (a) was not taken). The protection is the
default plus the fact that turning it on is a deliberate act. The test asserts
this override behavior explicitly, so if a guard is ever wanted, that
assertion is the one that must flip.

title: Auto-reindex wired only to gitnexus; default provider codebase-memory never re-indexes
description:
Auto-reindex is wired only to the provider that is being deprecated, and is
absent from the default provider.

- src/tools/code-intelligence-reindex.ts exports maybeScheduleReindex()
- The ONLY caller is src/tools/code-intelligence-gitnexus.ts:115
- src/tools/code-intelligence-codebase-memory.ts has 0 references
- The default provider is codebase-memory:
  src/tools/code-intelligence.ts:65 `let providerKey = 'codebase-memory';`

So on a default install, the partial update-phase coverage that apra-fleet-t0d
credits (staleness-triggered re-indexing) does not run at all. And
apra-fleet-0um.3 plans to register CodebaseMemoryProvider and deprecate
Joern/gitnexus, which would remove the only surface where it does run.

This is the concrete shape of the t0d.3 gap: the update phase is not merely
incomplete, it is attached to the wrong provider.

OPEN QUESTION: port maybeScheduleReindex into CodebaseMemoryProvider, or hoist
it above both providers into the shared getProvider()/handler layer so it is
provider-agnostic? The handler layer already hosts the other cross-cutting
concerns (recordUsage telemetry, enrichContextWithKb), which argues for
hoisting.

Done criteria:
- Auto-reindex fires on the default provider
- Placement decided (per-provider vs shared handler layer) and consistent with
  how recordUsage/enrichContextWithKb are placed
- Test coverage for the default-provider path, not just gitnexus

comments.author: kashhash
comments.text: DECISION (kashyapj, 2026-07-28): hoist maybeScheduleReindex to the SHARED handler layer, not into CodebaseMemoryProvider. Rationale: it sits alongside recordUsage and enrichContextWithKb, which are already cross-cutting concerns living in the tool-registry handlers rather than inside providers -- the design precedent is established and this keeps providers pure proxies (the stated P8/D8 and P4a/D4 rationale in the existing handler comments). One implementation, survives the Joern deprecation in apra-fleet-0um.3, and no new provider can forget to wire it. Remove the gitnexus-local call at code-intelligence-gitnexus.ts:115 as part of the move so it does not fire twice. Test coverage must exercise the DEFAULT provider path (codebase-memory), not just gitnexus.

title: fleet-sprint engine has no KB priming -- it lives only in the Claude workflow copy
description:
KB priming exists only in the Claude Code Workflow-tool copy, not in the
shipped fleet-sprint engine that README.md advertises.

Counts on the merged tree:
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ + packages/apra-fleet-se/src/ :
  0 references to kb_session_prime / kb_import / kbContext / primeKB
- packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js : 16

So `apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint ...` -- the headline command in
README.md "## Quick start" -- runs with no orchestrator-side KB context.
There is no primeKB() call and no `kbContext +` prefix on any dispatch.
The four agent contracts that carry a Step 0 block still self-prime, so the
feature is not entirely absent, but the injection layer (which is what makes
priming cheap and consistent across roles) is missing from the product path.

The KB port done in apra-fleet-iri put these features in the right place for
the Claude workflow. It did not, and was not scoped to, add them to the
engine.

OPEN QUESTION: is the engine deliberately KB-free (apra-pm workflow is the
intended home) or is this an unclosed gap? That decision sets the scope.

Done criteria:
- Decide: port kbContext injection + primeKB into the fleet-sprint engine, or
  document that the engine is intentionally KB-free and correct the README
- If porting: the 6 injection points that exist in auto-sprint.js (planner,
  doer claim, doer develop, reviewer, final-review, harvester) have engine
  equivalents
- A test asserting a fleet-sprint dispatch carries KB context
close_reason: fleet-sprint now primes the KB per member, resolving each member's work folder via member_detail and skipping any member whose folder cannot be resolved rather than priming against the fleet server cwd (which would reintroduce apra-fleet-tm7). Commit 2820749, 8 dedicated tests.

comments.author: kashhash
comments.text: DECISION (kashyapj, 2026-07-28): port priming INTO the fleet-sprint engine. Rationale: 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint' is the command README.md leads with in Quick start, so the flagship path cannot be the cold one. Scope: primeKB + the 6 kbContext injection points that already exist in packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js (planner, doer claim, doer develop, reviewer, final-review, harvester) get engine equivalents. Rejected: flag-gated port (defers the decision without reducing the work) and Step-0-only (repeats the prime call per role and gives no shared context). NOTE: this overlaps apra-fleet-6w7 -- orchestrator injection and per-role Step 0 are complementary, not alternatives; do both, but injection is the one that makes priming consistent across roles.

title: No automated kb_promote: unattended runs never contribute back to the team bible
description:
The KB confidence ladder has no automatic climb, so the git-shareable team
bible never populates in an unattended run.

The chain, verified on the merged tree:
- kb_capture CLAMPS to INFERRED. src/services/knowledge/sqlite-provider.ts:714
  appends "[confidence clamped: CONFIRMED requires kb_promote]".
- kb_harvest (auto-fires after every execute_prompt) writes UNVERIFIED.
- CONFIRMED is minted ONLY by kb_promote.
- kb_export exports ONLY CONFIRMED: src/tools/kb-export.ts:173
  `source.list({ confidence: 'CONFIRMED' })`.

Nothing calls kb_promote automatically. Grepped all four surfaces --
packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/*.md, the fleet-sprint engine
(packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/), the Claude workflow copy
(apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js), and src/ -- the only hits are
kb_promote's own implementation and prose describing it.

Consequence: an autonomous sprint accumulates UNVERIFIED + INFERRED entries
forever. .fleet/kb-canonical.json exports empty, so kb_import on another
machine/branch imports nothing, and the "git-shareable team bible" described
in README.md "## Knowledge Layer" and docs/knowledge-layer.md never
materialises without a human running kb_promote by hand. The KB is a
per-machine session cache today, not a shared knowledge asset.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION (needs a human decision before implementation):
who is allowed to promote? Candidates --
  a. harvester promotes at sprint end, gated on its own evidence
  b. reviewer promotes only what it independently validated
  c. mechanical threshold (survived N sessions / use_count / freshness)
  d. deliberately human-only, and the README/docs are what is wrong
Promotion feeds the git-committed bible, so this is a trust-boundary
decision, not just a wiring task.

Done criteria:
- Promotion policy decided and written down (docs/kb-trust-model.md is the
  likely home -- it already exists)
- Whatever is decided, README.md and docs/knowledge-layer.md match reality
- If automated: a test proving an unattended cycle produces a non-empty
  .fleet/kb-canonical.json
close_reason: reviewer.md Step 5 promote contract + Step 0 fix committed as bfc62e5 (not pushed)

comments.author: kashhash
comments.text: DECISION (kashyapj, 2026-07-28): the REVIEWER promotes, and only what it independently validated. Rationale: the reviewer is already a quality gate that verifies work against acceptance criteria, so routing promotion through it is the narrowest defensible expansion of trust -- no new judgment surface is introduced, an existing one is reused. Harvester-at-sprint-end was rejected as higher throughput but weaker per-entry evidence. Implementation notes: (1) reviewer.md gains a promote step scoped to entries whose claim it actually checked -- NOT a blanket promote-everything-touched; (2) kb_promote's existing directive refusal (sqlite-provider.ts:1110, human-terminal activation) must keep holding -- an agent promoting a pending user-directive stays forbidden; (3) needs a test proving an unattended cycle ends with a non-empty .fleet/kb-canonical.json, which is the acceptance signal for this whole bead.

comments.author: kashhash
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-07-28), supersedes the 'exports empty' claim in the original description.

The bible is NOT empty. .fleet/kb-canonical.json in this repo holds 97 entries, all CONFIRMED (78 knowledge, 14 learning, 3 runbook, 2 context-cache), and git history shows it growing: 89 -> 95 -> 97 across commits 6132f47, c33d3a6, 1da5bef, then two correction commits bc2904d and 91a65c8. So the export path demonstrably works and the bible is a live, git-reviewed artifact.

What survives from the original finding, verified by a whole-repo grep (the first grep was scoped to packages/apra-fleet-se/ and src/ only, which is why I missed the design docs):
- No CODE calls kb_promote. The only callers are humans/agents invoking the MCP tool directly in an interactive session.
- No role contract in packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/ mentions kb_promote.
- Neither the fleet-sprint engine nor the auto-sprint workflow triggers it.

So the accurate gap is narrower and different in kind: the bible BOOTSTRAPS fine (a fresh machine gets all 97 entries via kb_import from git) but an UNATTENDED sprint never contributes back to it. Knowledge learned autonomously stays at INFERRED/UNVERIFIED on the machine that learned it, forever.

Also note the reviewer-promotes decision is not new design -- it is the ORIGINAL design, already written down: docs/knowledge-layer-design.md:257 says 'Confirms doer learning -> kb_promote(id) -> INFERRED becomes CONFIRMED', and demo/demo-deck.html:81 says 'kb_promote to CONFIRMED only if the reviewer APPROVED'. This bead is closing a gap between documented design and shipped behavior, not inventing a policy.

Current KB state on this machine: ~/.apra-fleet/data/knowledge/ has both project and global directories but NO database files -- the live KB is cold/uninitialised. That makes it an ideal substrate for a real end-to-end proof.

title: Merge origin/main into feature branch and resolve conflicts
description:
Merge the latest origin/main into the current branch and resolve all conflicts, ensuring KB (Knowledge Bank) features survive the merge and land in the correct new locations.

## Background -- why this merge is non-trivial

origin/main commit 732dc38 retired the `vendor/apra-pm` git submodule. Its contents now live as plain files at `packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/`. Our branch added KB features to the OLD location (`vendor/apra-pm/`), which main deleted. A naive merge will accept main's deletion and silently drop all KB code.

The KB features that must survive:

1. **auto-sprint.js** -- KB priming and context injection
   - `KB_PRIMER_SCHEMA` constant (JSON schema for primer agent)
   - `_kbImported` flag (prevents re-importing each cycle)
   - `primeKB(repoPath)` function (dispatches haiku agent to call kb_session_prime + kb_import)
   - `buildKBContext(kbResult)` function (formats KB entries into a prompt block)
   - `kbContext` variable: initialized before the cycle loop, refreshed per cycle
   - 6 injection points where `kbContext +` is prepended to dispatch prompts:
     planner, doer (claim+develop), reviewer, final-review, harvester

2. **Agent definition files** -- Step 0 blocks

title: KB update phase: incremental re-indexing on code changes
description:
Implement the update phase: incremental re-indexing when code changes are detected. This should be triggered by the git post-commit hook (already installed by kb_setup) or lazily on the next code-intel tool call when staleness is detected.

Acceptance criteria:
- Post-commit hook triggers incremental re-index (or marks index as stale)
- code-intel tool calls detect stale index and trigger background re-index
- Re-indexing is incremental (only changed files), not full rebuild
- Stale index still serves results while re-indexing is in progress
- Re-index progress/completion is logged

title: KB init phase: first-time repo indexing with progress
description:

Acceptance criteria:
- kb_setup (or new kb_init) triggers first-time indexing for the repo
- Indexing reports progress (files indexed / total)
- On success, .apra-fleet/code-intel.json is written with enabled=true + indexedAt timestamp
- On failure, partial index is cleaned up and error is reported
- Re-running init on an already-indexed repo is a no-op (idempotent)
